candidates.source_name: Ephrem the Syrian / Commentary on the Psalms
candidates.source_attribution: Ephrem the Syrian, on Psalm 1. NPNF Series 2, vol. 13 (Gwynn). PD.
candidates.draft_body:
Ephrem the Syrian Commentary on the Psalms (c. 365 AD)

Ephrem opens his Psalter commentary with the threefold negation — walks not / stands not / sits not — as a progression of deepening complicity in evil: the walk is occasional, the standing is habitual, the sitting is settled. The Ethiopian Andəmta tradition develops this into a homiletic device for the daily examen, paired with the threefold ascent of the just (meditation by day / by night / yielding fruit in season).
candidates.reviewer_notes: Curated PD interpretive summary representing the Ethiopian Tewahedo tradition's reading via Ephrem the Syrian, Commentary on the Psalms.
